title: Teach Your Agent to Prove It's Done — Nick Nisi & Zack Proser, WorkOS
talk_summary: WorkOS workshop argues that agent reliability comes from making agents prove completion with deterministic, app-specific verifier CLIs and centralized verification services, then attaching evidence receipts to PRs. It recommends small outcome-defined tasks, CI-enforced checks, and detailed failure output so agents self-correct instead of self-reporting.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build an app-specific CLI that wraps browser/API/storage/DB checks so agents can run one deterministic command repeatedly until the app is proven working.
takeaways.evidence_quote: pinning it down to a single command that is backed by actual bash commands

takeaways.what_they_do: A web service receives agent completion claims over MCP, runs reusable verifiers against GitHub/artifacts, and either marks the workflow node satisfied or returns failing checks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: centralize authority for verification in a web service

takeaways.what_they_do: Require screenshots, videos, test results, smoke-test output, and recordings as proof attached to the PR, so reviewers inspect evidence before code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Show me the actual tangible proof that it actually did it

takeaways.what_they_do: Put the verification command in AGENTS.md and CI/hooks so every agent and PR runs it; do not rely on the model choosing a skill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having the CI actually enforce that these these commands get run

takeaways.what_they_do: Make failures explicit about why they failed and include detailed state so the agent can interpret the failure and self-heal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you make it so that your failure is explicit about why it failed and give as much detail as possible about how it got into that state

takeaways.what_they_do: Decompose work into small tasks and give each agent prompt the exact done state and verification method, avoiding giant multi-day sessions.
